lore_anchors.definition: A powerful “military path” weapon that corrupts a normal user’s personality with overwhelming bloodlust and aggression.

surfaces: True Sutra of the Fire Vestments
lore_anchors.definition: A sacred text of the Ao-Jing Sect; when recited, it produces a healing fire-slug that seals wounds with agonizing precision.
A government-sponsored supernormal law enforcement body that hunts rogue cultivators and manages supernatural disasters with near-total autonomy.
A steel striker used to ignite tinder; Li Huowang uses it to light talisman paper for divination.
A small cloth bag containing fragrant herbs, often worn as an accessory or given as a love token; in this chapter, it carries a hidden hexagram pattern.

cultural_notes_faq.a: An ancient Chinese practice where heated bones are cracked, and the fissures read as divine messages. Li Huowang uses a skull and a talisman manual for his version.

cultural_notes_faq.q: Why does Li Huowang torture the embroidery maiden so brutally?
cultural_notes_faq.a: He needs to determine if the suspect is telling the truth about the infant thefts. His methods are relentless but methodical, and he believes he can verify truth through extreme pain.

cultural_notes_faq.q: What does "connects the hexagram to the sachet" mean?
cultural_notes_faq.a: Li Huowang’s bone-divination produced a pattern that partially matches the embroidery on the magistrate’s daughter’s sachet. He interprets this as the oracle pointing toward the sachet’s maker.
